concept.title: Enterprise Agentic Memory, Bi-Temporal Knowledge Graphs & Decay

spark.summary: Scale agentic long-term memory across 50M+ namespaces without contradiction poisoning, HNSW post-filtering collapse, or slow GDPR erasure.
spark.keyTakeaway: If model quality drifts from offline training baselines, bi-Temporal Knowledge Graphs & Decay, pair a 3-tier memory hierarchy (Redis + Qdrant filterable HNSW + Neo4j bi-temporal KG) with async 8B SLM ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP conflict resolution, Ebbinghaus decay, and KMS DEK crypto-shredding.
spark.byteSummary:
Naive append-only vector stores collapse in enterprise agentic systems due to semantic contradiction poisoning (storing both 'User lives in NYC' and 'User moved to Seattle' with equal similarity) and multi-tenant HNSW post-filtering recall collapse.

An Enterprise Agentic Memory Engine solves this by separating a synchronous 3-way scatter-gather read path (<=25ms p99 across Redis Working RAM, Qdrant Int8 Filterable HNSW, and Neo4j/FalkorDB Bi-Temporal Knowledge Graph) from an asynchronous Kafka + 8B SLM write path (<=5ms ack).

Every extracted triplet is reconciled via deterministic ADD, UPDATE, DELETE, or NOOP mutations that close old valid-time windows (t_invalid = now()) without erasing audit lineage. At recall time, Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) and lazy Ebbinghaus decay R(t) = exp(-d*dt/(S*I)) surface fresh facts, while per-namespace KMS DEK crypto-shredding guarantees <=60s GDPR erasure.

learningJourney.title: Contradiction Poisoning & HNSW Post-Filtering Collapse
learningJourney.purpose: Understand why append-only vector databases fail as long-term agent memory.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Contradiction Poisoning & HNSW Post-Filtering Collapse** as the intuition layer for Enterprise Agentic Memory, Bi-Temporal Knowledge Graphs & Decay: Understand why append-only vector databases fail as long-term agent memory.
explanation.core: In an append-only vector store, updating a user's city from Seattle to Austin leaves both embeddings in the index, causing contradictory top-k retrieval. Furthermore, across 50M tenant namespaces, naive HNSW post-filtering retrieves global top-100 neighbors and then filters by tenant_id—returning zero matches when a tenant owns <0.001% of the corpus.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, contradiction poisoning & hnsw post-filtering collapse becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Principal design for 250K recall QPS across 100B facts: 8.5ms hedged scatter-gather reads, Int8 bitset HNSW, and <=60s KMS DEK crypto-shredding.

learningJourney.title: 3-Tier Memory Hierarchy (Working, Episodic, Bi-Temporal Graph)
learningJourney.purpose: Organize memory into Redis Working RAM, Qdrant Int8 HNSW, and Neo4j/FalkorDB KG.

explanation.foundation: Think of **3-Tier Memory Hierarchy (Working, Episodic, Bi-Temporal Graph)** as the intuition layer for Enterprise Agentic Memory, Bi-Temporal Knowledge Graphs & Decay: Organize memory into Redis Working RAM, Qdrant Int8 HNSW, and Neo4j/FalkorDB KG.

explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, 3-tier memory hierarchy (working, episodic, bi-temporal graph) becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Principal design for 250K recall QPS across 100B facts: 8.5ms hedged scatter-gather reads, Int8 bitset HNSW, and <=60s KMS DEK crypto-shredding.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Enterprise Agentic Memory, Bi-Temporal Knowledge Graphs & Decay without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: If model quality drifts from offline training baselines, bi-Temporal Knowledge Graphs & Decay, pair a 3-tier memory hierarchy (Redis + Qdrant filterable HNSW + Neo4j bi-temporal KG) with async 8B SLM ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP conflict resolution, Ebbinghaus decay, and KMS DEK crypto-shredding.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

learningJourney.title: Bi-Temporal Fact Model (t_valid vs t_created)
learningJourney.purpose: Track both world-time validity and system-time transactions for point-in-time audits.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Bi-Temporal Fact Model (t_valid vs t_created)** as the intuition layer for Enterprise Agentic Memory, Bi-Temporal Knowledge Graphs & Decay: Track both world-time validity and system-time transactions for point-in-time audits.
explanation.core: Every graph edge and fact carries four timestamps: t_valid and t_invalid (when the fact was true in the real world) plus t_created and t_deleted (when the system recorded it). Active queries automatically inject t_invalid IS NULL AND t_deleted IS NULL, while compliance audits can reconstruct exact agent knowledge at any historical timestamp without mutating history.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, bi-temporal fact model (t_valid vs t_created) becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Principal design for 250K recall QPS across 100B facts: 8.5ms hedged scatter-gather reads, Int8 bitset HNSW, and <=60s KMS DEK crypto-shredding.

assumptions: Assumes dual-timeline edge schema in Neo4j/FalkorDB

learningJourney.title: Async Kafka + 8B SLM Conflict Resolver (ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP)
learningJourney.purpose: Decouple 800ms LLM fact extraction from the <=5ms synchronous write acknowledgment.

explanation.foundation: Waiting for an LLM to extract triplets on the hot write path would add 800ms of blocking latency.
explanation.core: Instead, writes append to Tier 1 Redis and a Kafka ingestion topic in <=5ms.
explanation.deepDive: A fleet of 160 H100 GPUs running a distilled 8B SLM extracts (subject, predicate, object) triplets and reconciles them against existing facts using four atomic mutations: ADD, UPDATE, DELETE, or NOOP.

learningJourney.title: Lazy Ebbinghaus Decay & Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)
learningJourney.purpose: Rank retrieved memories by semantic relevance, graph proximity, and spaced-repetition decay.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Lazy Ebbinghaus Decay & Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)** as the intuition layer for Enterprise Agentic Memory, Bi-Temporal Knowledge Graphs & Decay: Rank retrieved memories by semantic relevance, graph proximity, and spaced-repetition decay.
explanation.core: Updating decay scores across 100B facts via nightly batch jobs is computationally impossible. Instead, Ebbinghaus retention R(t) = exp(-(d * dt) / (S * I)) is evaluated lazily at query re-ranking time over the top-k candidates returned by RRF, where dt is elapsed time since last recall, S is stability (incremented on recall), and I is intrinsic importance.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, lazy ebbinghaus decay & reciprocal rank fusion (rrf) becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Principal design for 250K recall QPS across 100B facts: 8.5ms hedged scatter-gather reads, Int8 bitset HNSW, and <=60s KMS DEK crypto-shredding.

assumptions: Assumes lazy evaluation at RRF re-ranking time
Assumes S increments on successful recall

learningJourney.title: Hedged Scatter-Gather Reads to Tame 3-Way Tail Amplification
learningJourney.purpose: Bound 3-way scatter-gather p99 latency under 25 ms despite independent tail skew.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Hedged Scatter-Gather Reads to Tame 3-Way Tail Amplification** as the intuition layer for Enterprise Agentic Memory, Bi-Temporal Knowledge Graphs & Decay: Bound 3-way scatter-gather p99 latency under 25 ms despite independent tail skew.
explanation.core: A parallel read across 3 tiers with independent 99% reliability suffers tail amplification: 1 - 0.99^3 = 2.97% of requests hit a tail delay. Dispatching a hedged read to a replica if any tier exceeds its p95 threshold (e.g., 8.5 ms) and cancelling the slower flight drops tail delay probability to ~0.12% for just ~5% extra read traffic.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, hedged scatter-gather reads to tame 3-way tail amplification becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Principal design for 250K recall QPS across 100B facts: 8.5ms hedged scatter-gather reads, Int8 bitset HNSW, and <=60s KMS DEK crypto-shredding.

assumptions: Assumes 3-way scatter-gather across Redis, Qdrant, Neo4j

codeExample.code:
import asyncio

async def hedged_tier_call(primary_coro, replica_coro, hedge_ms: float = 8.5):
    primary = asyncio.create_task(primary_coro())
    done, _ = await asyncio.wait({primary}, timeout=hedge_ms / 1000.0)
    if primary in done:
        return await primary
    replica = asyncio.create_task(replica_coro())
    done, pending = await asyncio.wait({primary, replica}, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
    for p in pending:
        p.cancel()
    return await next(iter(done))

learningJourney.title: Envelope Encryption & <=60s GDPR DEK Crypto-Shredding
learningJourney.purpose: Achieve instant 'Right to be Forgotten' erasure without rebuilding 115 TB HNSW graphs.

explanation.foundation: Re-indexing 115 TB of HNSW graphs on disk for every GDPR deletion request is impossible.
explanation.core: Instead, every namespace's payloads and graph attributes are encrypted with a dedicated KMS Data Encryption Key (DEK).
explanation.deepDive: A GDPR purge deletes Tier 1 Redis keys in <=100ms, schedules async Qdrant/Neo4j payload purges, and zeroizes the namespace's KMS DEK—rendering all disk and snapshot copies permanently unreadable within 60 seconds.

assumptions: Assumes per-namespace KMS DEK envelope encryption

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does naive HNSW post-filtering fail when serving 50M+ isolated agent namespaces?

options.text: Post-filtering traverses the global HNSW graph first and filters by tenant_id afterward, returning zero results for small tenants
options.feedback: Correct. If a tenant owns <0.001% of vectors, global top-k neighbors belong to other tenants and get stripped out.

options.text: HNSW does not support floating-point cosine distance
options.feedback: HNSW natively supports cosine, dot-product, and L2 distances.

options.text: Post-filtering encrypts vectors with the wrong KMS DEK
options.feedback: Encryption happens at rest on payloads, not during HNSW distance comparisons.

options.text: Post-filtering forces Redis Cluster to evict working memory
options.feedback: Redis Tier 1 operates independently from Qdrant's HNSW index.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Filterable HNSW evaluates tenant bitset masks during graph traversal so every visited candidate belongs to the target namespace.

knowledgeChecks.question: When a user states 'I moved from NYC to Seattle', how does the 8B SLM Conflict Resolver update the bi-temporal knowledge graph?

options.text: It executes a hard DELETE on the NYC node and erases all historical traces
It issues an UPDATE mutation that sets t_invalid = now() on the NYC edge and inserts a new Seattle edge with t_valid = now()
options.feedback: Correct. Closing t_invalid on the old edge resolves contradictions for active queries while preserving historical lineage.

options.text: It issues a NOOP so both cities remain equally active
options.feedback: Leaving both active causes contradiction poisoning.

options.text: It triggers a full HNSW index rebuild across all 120 Qdrant shards
options.feedback: Graph updates are localized mutations, never full index rebuilds.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Bi-temporal UPDATE mutations close the prior valid-time interval without destroying audit history.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does the engine achieve <=60s GDPR 'Right to be Forgotten' erasure without rewriting 115 TB of HNSW files?

options.text: By lowering the Ebbinghaus decay constant d to zero
options.feedback: Zero decay would actually preserve memories forever.

options.text: By setting Redis tombstones and destroying the namespace's KMS Data Encryption Key (crypto-shredding)
options.feedback: Correct. Zeroizing the per-namespace DEK renders all stored payloads and disk snapshots permanently unreadable within 60 seconds.

options.text: By pausing Kafka ingestion for 72 hours
options.feedback: Pausing ingestion breaks live writes for all tenants.

options.text: By running 8.5 ms hedged reads on every replica
options.feedback: Hedged reads reduce tail latency, not data retention.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Envelope encryption with per-namespace KMS DEKs makes cryptographic erasure instantaneous across live storage and backups.

beginner.summary: Learn how AI agents remember user facts across months without mixing up old and new information or leaking data between users.
beginner.keyTakeaway: If model quality drifts from offline training baselines, Bi-Temporal Knowledge Graphs & Decay, pair a 3-tier memory hierarchy (Redis + Qdrant filterable HNSW + Neo4j bi-temporal KG) with async 8B SLM ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP conflict resolution, Ebbinghaus decay, and KMS DEK crypto-shredding.
beginner.byteSummary:
An AI assistant needs more than a chat history—if a user moves to a new city, the agent must remember the new city while knowing the old one is outdated.

Enterprise memory engines use three layers: fast RAM for the current chat, a vector database for past conversations, and a knowledge graph that tracks when each fact started and stopped being true.

Background models clean up contradictions automatically, and per-user encryption keys allow instant deletion for privacy laws like GDPR.

intermediate.summary: Build a 3-tier memory engine (Redis, Qdrant filterable HNSW, Neo4j bi-temporal KG) with async Kafka 8B SLM conflict resolution and lazy Ebbinghaus decay.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: If model quality drifts from offline training baselines, Bi-Temporal Knowledge Graphs & Decay, pair a 3-tier memory hierarchy (Redis + Qdrant filterable HNSW + Neo4j bi-temporal KG) with async 8B SLM ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP conflict resolution, Ebbinghaus decay, and KMS DEK crypto-shredding.
intermediate.byteSummary:
Scaling agent memory to millions of namespaces requires a synchronous 3-way read path (Redis <=3ms, Qdrant Int8 HNSW <=12ms, Neo4j <=15ms) and an asynchronous Kafka + 8B SLM write path.

The SLM emits ADD, UPDATE, DELETE, or NOOP mutations against bi-temporal edges (t_valid, t_invalid). Lazy Ebbinghaus decay R(t) = exp(-d*dt/(S*I)) re-ranks results at query time without batch sweeps.

advanced.summary: Principal design for 250K recall QPS across 100B facts: 8.5ms hedged scatter-gather reads, Int8 bitset HNSW, and <=60s KMS DEK crypto-shredding.

advanced.byteSummary:
At 250K recall QPS across 50M namespaces, 3-way scatter-gather amplifies p99 tail delay to 1 - 0.99^3 = 2.97%. Dispatching 8.5ms hedged reads cuts tail delay to ~0.12% for ~5% extra QPS, while Tier 3 circuit breakers degrade gracefully to Tier 1+2.

Per-namespace KMS DEKs allow <=100ms Redis tombstoning and <=60s crypto-shredding without rebuilding 115 TB of Int8 HNSW graphs.
